subject: AI & Agents
title: AI Doesn't Learn Like You Do
description: A quick, practical guide to AI Doesn't Learn Like You Do.

hook.text: Show a child one cat and it knows all cats. Show AI 10,000 cats and it still misses cats in costumes.

buildup.text: Humans learn from tiny amounts of data using prior knowledge, analogies, and embodied experience.

discovery.text: AI learns statistical correlations from massive datasets, not conceptual understanding from experience.

twist.text: This is why AI can ace a medical exam but not understand why a patient is scared of needles.

climax.text: Few-shot learning bridges some of this gap, but fundamental differences in learning remain vast.

punchline.text: Ten thousand examples to learn what a toddler gets in one.

quiz.question: How does human learning fundamentally differ from AI learning?
options: Humans learn from minimal data using prior knowledge and experience
Humans and AI learn in exactly the same way
Humans require more data than AI to learn

details.summary: AI learning involves adjusting numerical weights through mathematical optimization, nothing like human learning through experience, reasoning, and emotional engagement. The word 'learning' is a metaphor.
details.whyItMatters: Calling it learning creates expectations that AI understands, grows, and reasons as humans do. Recognizing the metaphor prevents misplaced trust in AI capabilities.
takeaways: AI 'learning' means adjusting numerical parameters via optimization
Humans learn through experience, reasoning, and emotion
The learning metaphor creates misleading expectations about AI

faq.question: How does machine learning differ from human learning?
faq.answer: Machine learning adjusts model weights by minimizing error on training data. Human learning involves understanding, reasoning, emotional engagement, and transferring knowledge flexibly to new situations.

faq.question: Why is the term 'learning' used for AI if it is different?
faq.answer: It is an intuitive metaphor borrowed by early researchers. The system does improve at tasks through exposure to data, which loosely parallels learning. But the mechanisms are fundamentally different.
